speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to your consultation. I see you have a history of delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and bone fragility; to understand the underlying cause, have you been diagnosed with any conditions like osteoporosis, Marfan syndrome, or Fragile X syndrome previously?

Also, have you experienced frequent fractures from minor injuries or heard about your family members having similar bone issues?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency). The combination of ambiguous genitalia at birth, hirsutism, severe acne, delayed menarche, and bone fragility suggests chronic androgen excess. REQUEST TEST: 17-hydroxyprogesterone, ACTH stimulation test. REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_ultrasound.
